source_caption:
Frances Ha feels so natural because Greta Gerwig didn’t just star in it — she co-wrote the film with Noah Baumbach, shaping Frances around a very specific kind of messy, funny, early-adult uncertainty. The black-and-white style makes her small New York struggles feel almost cinematic and timeless, like a French New Wave heroine who still can’t quite pay rent.

Frances Ha (2012), directed by Noah Baumbach, starring Greta Gerwig, Mickey Sumner, Adam Driver. A charming and bittersweet indie comedy about friendship, ambition, and feeling lost in your twenties, capturing the awkward beauty of becoming yourself before you know where life is going.

source_details.title: Frances Ha
source_details.synopsis: Frances Ha is a 2012 American comedy drama film directed by Noah Baumbach. It is written by Baumbach and Greta Gerwig, who also stars as Frances, a struggling 27-year-old dancer whose career and social life begin imploding at the same time that her best friend's life begins taking off. The film premiered at the Telluride Film Festival on September 1, 2012, and was given a limited theatrical release in the United States on May 17, 2013, by IFC Films.
